research.domain: Observability + SLO + Operational Readiness (metrics/TSDB, tracing, SLO-gated delivery, incident/on-call culture, OTel posture, audit vs ops logging)

per_company.approach: Doctrine: SRE book golden signals (latency/traffic/errors/saturation) + SLO/error-budget governance; SRE Workbook 'Alerting on SLOs' prescribes multiwindow multi-burn-rate paging as the terminal iteration: page at 14.4x burn over 1h (2% of 30d budget) and 6x over 6h (5%), ticket at 1x over 3d (10%), each paired with a short control window (5m/30m/6h) to stop stale firing. Metrics substrate: Monarch (VLDB 2020) — planet-scale in-memory TSDB, ~1 PB compressed in memory, terabytes/sec ingest, millions of queries/sec, regionalized ingest/storage with a global query+config plane; push-based collection (deliberate retirement of pull-based Borgmon and its per-team config sprawl); alert evaluation pushed down to leaf nodes so alerting survives partitions; typed relational time-series schema enables static query analysis. Dogfooding is structural: Cloud Monitoring and Managed Service for Prometheus are the SAME Monarch backend Google uses internally (24-month metric retention). Tracing: Dapper — head-based sampling, originally uniform 1/1024 (−0.20% latency, −0.06% throughput overhead at that rate), evolved to adaptive rate-per-unit-time sampling; >1 TB sampled trace data/day. Deployments: SRE Workbook 'Canarying Releases' codifies canary evaluation against SLO metrics before fleet-wide rollout. Audit: Cloud Audit Logs Admin Activity logs are always-on (cannot be disabled or excluded), immutable, fixed 400-day retention in the _Required bucket, separate from operational Cloud Logging. OTel: co-founder lineage (OpenCensus), OTel/PromQL are the public interop surface over Monarch.

CloudWatch scale (re:Invent 2025, COP328): 20 quadrillion metric observations/month, 13 EB logs/month, 455 B traces/month, 861 M synthetic canary runs/month; Amazon runs its own ops on CloudWatch. Builders' Library 'Instrumenting distributed systems' (Yanacek): one structured log entry per unit of work is the telemetry primitive; aggregate metrics are computed from logs after the fact (EMF pattern); alarm/operate on p99/p99.9/p99.99, never averages; Contributor Insights handles high-cardinality analysis outside the metric store. Builders' Library 'Automating safe, hands-off deployments' (Liguori): every microservice per region has a high-severity aggregate alarm that both pages on-call AND auto-rolls-back in-flight deployments — rollback typically underway before the human engages; pipelines are fully hands-off with one-box → wave-based regional rollout and bake times. Operational readiness: ORR is a formal, curated checklist mechanism distilled from incident learnings, required before launch; COE (Correction of Error) is the closed-loop post-incident analysis, and COE templates explicitly inspect ORR efficacy ('would any ORR recommendation have avoided this?') — incidents feed the checklist. Tracing: X-Ray's static head-based sampling rules are being retired; AWS announced (Nov 2025) OpenTelemetry as the primary instrumentation standard, ADOT supports tail-based sampling, and Transaction Search offers 100% trace capture without sampling; CloudWatch added OTLP metrics ingestion (2026). Audit: CloudTrail is a separate service from CloudWatch Logs; log-file integrity validation via SHA-256 hash chains + RSA-signed hourly digest files (tamper-evident), CloudTrail Lake retention configurable to 10 years.

Metrics: ODS (Operational Data Store) with Gorilla (VLDB 2015) as the in-memory hot tier — write-through cache over HBase, 26-hour in-memory window, XOR delta-of-delta compression averaging 12x, ~700 M data points/minute across ~2 B unique time series at publication; open-sourced as Beringei. High-cardinality/exploratory tier: Scuba — distributed in-memory columnar store for near-real-time arbitrary slicing (regression analysis, ads revenue, perf debugging); the metrics store stays bounded because exploration happens in Scuba, not in ODS labels. Tracing: Canopy (SOSP 2017) — 1.3 B traces/day spanning browser/mobile/backend, per-dataset customizable sampling and feature extraction into 129+ derived performance datasets; traces are an analytics input, not just waterfall views. Deployment: Conveyor (OSDI 2023) — single company-wide CD tool; 97% of container service pipelines fully automated (55% true continuous deployment, 42% scheduled), gated by the Health Check Service (HCS) evaluating user-defined anomaly rules (including product metrics like engagement) during rollout, plus dependency analysis to block faulty releases. Incident culture: SEV levels with blameless SEV reviews — recurring company-wide and org-level review meetings with SEV owner, SEV experts, and stakeholders; 'more SEVs reported = healthier reporting culture' framing; timeline-driven retros producing tracked follow-ups. OTel: no public adoption — internal proprietary instrumentation throughout.

Internal substrate: Geneva — agent-based pipeline with hot path (MDM multi-dimensional metrics + health alerts, <60 s time-to-decision), warm path (logs/diagnostics/tracing, ~5 min), cold path (long-term storage). Published scale: >2 B metrics/min AFTER client-side pre-aggregation, >500 M unique time series/min, >5 PB logs/day, 99% of metric queries <500 ms. Cardinality is hard-capped: Azure Monitor/MDM-style limits (e.g., 5,000 time series per metric per 24h, overflow series replaced with sentinel 'Maximum values reached'; per-dimension unique-value caps with 'Other values' bucket). Azure Monitor is the externalized Geneva lineage; Geneva agents remain Microsoft-tenant-only. Log analytics: Kusto/Azure Data Explorer — grassroots internal tool that virtually all Microsoft products now use (largest internal table ~200 B records/day, ~1.6 PB/day raw, 14-day troubleshooting retention); backs Azure Monitor Logs, Sentinel, M365 Defender — deep dogfooding. Deployments: Safe Deployment Practices (Russinovich) — mandatory health signals and mandatory bake times between ring stages, internal/self-host rings before production, >1 week full rollout, automatic rollback to last-known-healthy; Gandalf AIOps layer uses ML to correlate faults and make rollout/rollback decisions by impact scope/severity. Incidents: Post-Incident Reviews (PIRs) published on Azure status history. OTel: Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro is the recommended path; App Insights Classic SDK deprecated (retires 2027). Audit: Activity Log 90-day default then export; compliance pattern is diagnostic-settings export to WORM-immutable Blob storage; Purview Audit Premium up to 10 years.

Public o11y suite: OCI Monitoring (metrics + alarms), Logging, Log Analytics (indexing/anomaly/RCA tier), APM with OpenTelemetry/OTLP instrumentation support plus OpenTracing/OpenMetrics compatibility, synthetic + real-user monitoring. Audit: OCI Audit service is on by default with a fixed tenancy-wide 365-day retention (the strictest fixed default among the five); longer retention via export to Object Storage. Dogfooding/self-monitoring: 'Behind the Scenes: OCI's Thousand-Eyed Canary' — an internal canary fleet continuously exercising telemetry and service endpoints in every OCI region, surfaced through a single global internal operations console. Change safety: all changes including planned maintenance deploy sequentially across regional pairs within a realm — primary region updated first, health of changed resources monitored for a minimum validation period before the secondary region is touched, ensuring only one region of a pair is under active change at any time. Less is published about OCI's internal TSDB internals than the other four; their public posture leans standards-first (CNCF, OTel, Grafana/PagerDuty integrations).

convergent_patterns: Metrics-gated progressive delivery with AUTOMATIC rollback is universal (5/5): AWS high-severity alarms auto-roll-back mid-deployment before the human is paged; Azure SDP rings with mandatory health signals + bake times + Gandalf AIOps rollback; Meta Conveyor's Health Check Service gates 97%-automated pipelines; Google canary evaluation against SLO metrics; OCI monitors a primary region for a minimum validation period before touching its pair. Nobody ships hyperscaler control planes with human-watched deploys.

Wave/ring/cell-scoped blast radius for every change (5/5): one-box → waves (AWS), internal → self-host → production rings over >1 week (Azure), phased tiers (Meta), canary populations (Google), one-region-of-a-pair-at-a-time (OCI). Bake time between stages is mandatory policy, not convention.

Two-tier telemetry split: a bounded-cardinality, in-memory/hot-path metrics store for alerting (<60 s decision) plus a separate high-cardinality columnar event/log store for exploration — Monarch + Cloud Logging/BigQuery, Gorilla/ODS + Scuba, Geneva MDM hot path + Kusto/ADX, CloudWatch metrics + Logs Insights/Contributor Insights, OCI Monitoring + Log Analytics. High-cardinality questions are answered by the event store, never by exploding metric labels.

Cardinality is controlled by hard enforcement, not advice (4+): Geneva/Azure caps series-per-metric with sentinel overflow values; Monarch's typed schemas + Borgmon retirement were explicitly motivated by config/cardinality sprawl; Amazon derives metrics from structured logs so the metric space stays curated while logs keep full fidelity; Meta routes unbounded dimensions to Scuba.

Per-unit-of-work structured wide events as the instrumentation primitive (3+): Amazon's one-log-entry-per-request with after-the-fact metric derivation; Scuba rows; Canopy traces feeding derived performance datasets. Metrics become a projection of events, preserving re-aggregation ability.

SLO/error-budget + multiwindow multi-burn-rate alerting as the paging doctrine: authored by Google (SRE Workbook 14.4x/1h, 6x/6h page; 1x/3d ticket), productized in Google Cloud SLO monitoring and AWS CloudWatch Application Signals SLOs, and embedded in Azure/AWS Well-Architected operational guidance. Cause-based static-threshold paging is the explicitly retired predecessor.

Closed-loop incident mechanism feeding a launch-readiness checklist (4+): AWS COE explicitly audits ORR coverage and incidents update the ORR question bank; Meta SEV reviews generate tracked follow-ups in recurring review meetings; Google postmortem culture feeds launch/production-readiness reviews; Azure PIRs feed SDP policy. Operational readiness is a versioned, evolving artifact derived from incidents — not a one-time gate.

Blameless, severity-leveled incident review as a first-class engineering ritual (4+): Meta SEV culture ('more reported SEVs = healthier org'), AWS COE, Google blameless postmortems, Azure PIR — all with named owners, timelines, and action items tracked to closure.

OpenTelemetry as the external/customer instrumentation standard (4/5): AWS declared OTel primary for X-Ray (2025) + OTLP into CloudWatch; Azure Monitor OTel Distro is the recommended path with Classic SDK retirement; Google's OpenCensus lineage + OTLP/PromQL surfaces; OCI APM ingests OTel. Internal hot paths remain proprietary everywhere — OTel is the edge contract, not the internal bus.

The public o11y product IS the internal stack (dogfooding, 4+): Cloud Monitoring/Managed Prometheus run on Monarch itself; Azure Monitor is externalized Geneva lineage and Azure Monitor Logs runs on Kusto which all of Microsoft dogfoods; Amazon operates on CloudWatch (20 quadrillion obs/month includes Amazon itself); OCI's canary fleet exercises its own telemetry services in every region.

Self-monitoring is out-of-band by design: Monarch evaluates alerts at leaf nodes so partitions can't blind paging and regionalizes ingest for failure isolation; OCI runs an independent thousand-eyed canary fleet probing every region; AWS runs 861 M synthetic canary runs/month; alerting must not depend on the global query plane being healthy.

Audit logging is a separate, immutable, can't-be-disabled lane distinct from operational logging (4+): CloudTrail (SHA-256 hash-chained signed digests) vs CloudWatch Logs; GCP Admin Activity audit logs always-on/immutable/fixed 400-day _Required bucket vs Cloud Logging; OCI Audit fixed 365-day tenancy-wide vs OCI Logging; Azure Activity Log + WORM blob export vs Log Analytics.
divergences: Trace sampling strategy: Google Dapper is head-based adaptive (uniform 1/1024 origin; overhead-driven rationale) and accepts statistical loss; AWS is moving the opposite direction — Transaction Search offers 100% trace capture without sampling plus ADOT tail-based sampling (storage economics changed, customers demand exemplar completeness); Azure App Insights uses client-side adaptive sampling (SDK cost focus); Meta Canopy makes sampling a per-dataset, user-customized policy because trace consumers want different fidelity. There is no industry consensus — the consensus is only that the sampling decision must be policy-configurable per use case.

Push vs pull metrics collection: Google deliberately retired pull-based Borgmon for push-based Monarch (config sprawl, scale robustness), while simultaneously backing pull-based Prometheus semantics externally via Managed Service for Prometheus on the same backend; AWS/Geneva use agent-local pre-aggregation then push. Pull survives as an ecosystem-compatibility surface, push wins inside planet-scale substrates.

Logs-first vs metrics-first: Amazon computes metrics from per-request structured logs after the fact (full fidelity, re-aggregatable, higher pipeline cost); Geneva MDM and Meta ODS pre-aggregate at the client/agent for <60 s hot-path decisions (cheap, fast, lossy). This is a genuine latency-vs-fidelity tradeoff both sides defend.

Rollback decisioning: AWS uses deterministic, pre-declared alarms (predictable, auditable); Azure layers ML/AIOps (Gandalf) to infer impact scope and decide rollout/rollback (catches unknown-unknowns, less explainable); Meta HCS uses user-defined anomaly rules including product metrics (engagement drops). Determinism vs learned judgment is unresolved.

Audit retention philosophy: fixed and non-negotiable (OCI 365 days tenancy-wide; GCP 400 days immutable, cannot disable) vs customer-configurable responsibility (AWS CloudTrail Lake up to 10 years, you choose; Azure 90-day default, export-to-WORM is your job). Disagreement over whether compliance-grade retention is the platform's duty or the customer's.

OpenTelemetry internally: Meta abstains entirely (no public OTel adoption; Canopy/ODS proprietary end-to-end) while the four clouds converged on OTel as the external standard — Meta has no external cloud customers, confirming OTel's value is the customer-facing contract, not internal efficiency.

Trace volume economics: Google publishes that 1/1024 sampling was acceptable for diagnosis; AWS now sells 100% capture; Meta keeps 1.3 B traces/day but only because derived-dataset extraction makes them queryable. The disagreement is whether raw traces or extracted features are the durable artifact.
anti_patterns: Per-team monitoring configuration sprawl: Google explicitly retired Borgmon partly because every team hand-maintaining collection/alerting configs didn't scale organizationally — Monarch centralized schema, collection, and query into one managed substrate.

Human-watched deployments and manual rollback: AWS pipelines are 'completely hands-off' by policy; Meta reports 97% of container pipelines have zero manual intervention. A human staring at dashboards during deploy is a retired practice.

Proprietary instrumentation SDKs at the edge: AWS deprecated the X-Ray SDKs/daemon in favor of OTel (2025); Microsoft deprecated App Insights Classic SDK (retires 2027) for the OTel Distro. Building a bespoke client instrumentation API in 2026 is an explicitly abandoned position.

Averages and static thresholds: Amazon instruments p99/p99.9/p99.99 because means hide tail pain; the SRE Workbook's alerting chapter is literally structured as the progressive retirement of static target-error-rate and cause-based alerts in favor of burn-rate alerts.

Unbounded metric cardinality: Azure Monitor/Geneva hard-cap series per metric and replace overflow with sentinel values rather than let the TSDB degrade; tenant/user/request IDs as metric dimensions is the canonical failure everyone routes to the event store instead.
One deployment tool per team: Meta's Conveyor paper is titled 'One-Tool-Fits-All' precisely because fragmented per-team deploy tooling made change-safety unenforceable.

Mixing audit and operational logging in one pipeline: every cloud that sells compliance separates them (CloudTrail/Cloud Audit Logs/OCI Audit are distinct services with independent immutability and retention) — audit trails sharing the ops-log retention knobs or deletion paths is a retired design.

Monitoring that depends on the monitored system's health: global-query-plane-dependent alerting is avoided — Monarch evaluates alerts at leaves, OCI/AWS run independent out-of-band canary fleets; in-band-only self-observation is a known single point of blindness.

ORR as a one-time launch gate: AWS treats the ORR as a living question bank continuously amended by COEs; a static pre-launch checklist that never ingests incident learnings is the named failure mode their mechanism exists to prevent.
oyatie_prescriptions: Make OpenSLO files (already mandated at {oya,cloud}/<service>/slos/*.openslo.yaml per ADR-0130) the single source from which alerting is CODEGENERATED: a buck2 rule compiles each SLO into the Google SRE Workbook multiwindow multi-burn-rate set — page on 14.4x burn over 1h AND 5m, page on 6x over 6h AND 30m, ticket on 1x over 3d AND 6h — and the cloud-ci admission gate rejects any hand-written static-threshold paging alert. This is the only paging policy; cause-based alerts may exist but may not page.

Wire burn-rate alarms as the automatic rollback trigger in the oya-ci/Tide promotion pipeline (AWS hands-off model): every service declares one high-severity aggregate alarm per cell; during a rollout, alarm breach auto-rolls-back BEFORE paging; mandatory bake times between waves (Azure SDP). Sequence waves along the ADR-0341/0348 cell topology — one cell → remaining cells in one AZ/region → region pairs (OCI model) — so shuffle-sharded cells are the natural blast-radius unit. The o11y and IdP/Cedar control planes ride the SLOWEST wave schedule.

Standardize Rust/axum instrumentation on one structured wide event per unit of work (tower middleware emitting a canonical request record: trace_id, cell_id, tenant_id, Cedar policy/decision id, timers, counters) and DERIVE golden-signal/RED metrics from these events after the fact (Amazon EMF model). Never hand-maintain parallel counters that can drift from the event record. Alarm on p99/p99.9, never averages.

Enforce metric cardinality budgets at build time: metric families are declared in a schema file under the service directory, codegen'd via buck2 into typed Rust registration (Monarch's typed-schema lesson), with a per-metric max-series cap enforced at the ingest tier using Geneva-style sentinel overflow ('Maximum values reached') rather than silent OOM. Hard rule: tenant_id, user_id, request_id are FORBIDDEN as metric labels — tenant-granular questions are answered by the event store. cell_id and region ARE first-class mandatory labels.

Build the telemetry substrate as two explicit tiers in cloud/observability/: (1) a cell-local hot metrics path — Prometheus-compatible TSDB with Gorilla XOR compression and a ~26h in-memory window, alert evaluation executed CELL-LOCALLY so a partition cannot blind paging (Monarch leaf-evaluation), with a thin global query/federation plane for cross-cell views; (2) a columnar wide-event store (Scuba/Kusto-class, e.g. ClickHouse-engine) holding the structured request events with 14–30 day retention for high-cardinality exploration, regression hunting, and per-tenant forensics. Multi-tenant SaaS debugging lives in tier 2, never in metric labels.

OTel posture: OTLP/W3C TraceContext is the ONLY external ingestion contract for the o11y product (matching AWS/Azure/Google/OCI convergence and CNCF graduation), even if internal hot paths use bespoke encodings. Tracing default: head-based adaptive sampling per service (Dapper), plus a tail-sampling collector tier that keeps 100% of error and p99-latency traces; 100% unsampled capture for all control-plane mutations and Cedar deny decisions (AWS Transaction Search precedent shows full capture is now economically viable).

Stand up the audit lane as a separate single-concern service (per ADR-0132 no-grouping) completely disjoint from operational logging: control-plane mutations, IdP auth events, and Cedar authorization decisions are written as hash-chained, signed digest batches (CloudTrail integrity model) to WORM object storage; minimum 365-day retention, fixed, non-configurable, non-disableable by tenants OR operators (OCI/GCP precedent). Ops logs stay on cheap 14–90 day retention. This separation is a launch blocker for the multi-tenant SaaS compliance story, not a fast-follow.

Operational readiness as code in the governance pipeline: a machine-readable ORR checklist (runbook URL per alert — admission fails without it; tested rollback; SLO files present; dashboard links; on-call rotation declared; meta-monitoring registered) evaluated by the existing cloud-ci gates before any service promotes past dev, extending ADR-0130. Pair it with a COE/SEV-style closed loop: blameless post-incident docs with severity levels, action items tracked to verified closure through the same PR-based governance pipeline, and the COE template asking the AWS question — 'would any ORR item have prevented this?' — with answers amending the checklist.

Meta-monitor the o11y stack from outside itself: each cell's o11y components are monitored by a DIFFERENT cell/region (Monarch self-hosting layering), plus an independent out-of-band canary/probe fleet continuously exercising every cell's public endpoints including the o11y product's own ingest and query APIs (OCI thousand-eyed canary; AWS runs 861M canary executions/month). The o11y stack must also be tenant zero of Oyatie's own IdP and billing — dogfooding the full SaaS path, mirroring Monarch↔Cloud Monitoring and Geneva↔Azure Monitor.

Adopt the burn-rate vocabulary in the product surface itself: since Oyatie sells an o11y substrate, ship SLO objects, error-budget policies, and multiwindow burn-rate alerts as first-class product primitives (as Google Cloud SLO monitoring and AWS Application Signals now do) rather than leaving customers to assemble them from raw alarms — this is where the four clouds converged their managed offerings between 2021–2026.

research.domain: Internal delivery fabric / developer platform (pipeline-as-product): monorepo SCM, submit/merge-queue mechanics, presubmit/postsubmit CI, build determinism + remote execution, large-scale change automation, deployment-pipeline doctrine, and developer-productivity metrics at AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle

per_company.approach: Piper (bespoke centralized monorepo VCS on Spanner, replicated across 10 DCs via Paxos): ~1B files, 2B LOC, 86TB, 35M commits; ~40-45k commits/workday of which ~24k from automated systems vs ~16k human (CACM 2016). Developers use CitC (Clients-in-the-Cloud): FUSE filesystem overlaying edits on the full repo; average workspace has <10 modified files — working copies are virtual, not cloned. TAP (Test Automation Platform) is the CI gateway: >50,000 unique changes/day, >4 billion test executions/day. Presubmit = curated fast subset chosen from the near-real-time global dependency graph; ~11 min average submission latency; a presubmit pass predicts 95%+ probability of passing all affected tests. Postsubmit runs ALL potentially affected tests asynchronously in batches (cannot run every test per change); failing batches are automatically split and re-run per-change for culprit finding, and TAP auto-rolls-back changes when it has high confidence in the culprit. Build Cop role per team keeps trunk green; rollback-first culture. Blaze/Bazel + Forge remote execution with content-addressed action caching underpins all of this. Critique code review: LGTM + owner approval + no unresolved comments required to commit; Tricorder static-analysis fleet surfaces findings as chips in review — ~93,000 findings/day across ~30 categories, ~5,000 builds/day, with a hard quality bar: effective false-positive / 'not useful' click rate held under ~5% or the analyzer is removed (ICSE 2015 paper). Rosie executes large-scale changes: shards a mass change by ownership boundaries into atomically-submittable pieces, runs each through an independent test-mail-submit pipeline, routes to OWNERS or to 'global approvers' who use pattern-based tooling to auto-approve conforming shards. Productivity steering: GSM (Goals/Signals/Metrics) + QUANTS (Quality, Attention, Intellectual complexity, Tempo, Satisfaction) — explicitly multidimensional, survey + logs, never single activity metrics (SWE book ch7).

Sapling SCM (client) + Mononoke (Rust, scalable distributed source-control server, in production) + EdenFS (virtual FS: checkout in seconds, files fetched lazily on access) for repos with millions of files and thousands of developers. Buck2 (Rust rewrite of Buck) with remote execution + remote caching so 'developers share each other's compilations' and one developer can fan out to thousands of machines; deep integration with Watchman/EdenFS so it works with files not on disk. Workflow: stacked diffs (series of small dependent changes) reviewed in Phabricator (internal fork); Sandcastle CI runs at diff time (2015 figures: >1,000 test results/sec, ~5 machine-years of work/day across thousands of machines in 5 DCs); Herald→Butterflybot rules engine automates review actions (e.g., flag deprecated APIs). Predictive Test Selection (MLSys 2019): ML model trained on historical test outcomes selects ~1/3 of transitively-affected tests yet catches >99.9% of regressions before they hit trunk — doubled testing-infra efficiency. Landcastle is the land queue: rebases, re-tests before/after landing; failures file tasks that can be 'push blocking' — code does not ship until resolved. Release doctrine: moved from cherry-pick release branches to push-from-master (2017 'Rapid release at massive scale'): 2% canary with continuous monitoring then 100%. Conveyor (OSDI 2023): one-tool-fits-all deployment managing 30,000+ pipelines; 97% of container-service pipelines are fully automated with no manual intervention (55% continuous per-change deploy, 42% scheduled daily/weekly). Mobile CD paper (FSE 2016): Android cadence 8 weeks→1 week; 20x team and 50x codebase growth without productivity/quality loss.

Explicitly polyrepo: thousands of small packages built by Brazil, which resolves interface-version dependencies against immutable 'version sets'; builds are hermetic (nothing depended on beyond GCC/glibc + declared deps, controlled linker/classpaths) and the system 'guarantees the ability to reproduce any artifact that has ever been produced' and produce any artifact with a known delta. Apollo deployment engine: 50M deployments to dev/test/prod hosts in 12 months (2014) — more than one per second; symlink-tree environments isolate coexisting versions per host. Pipelines doctrine (Builders' Library, Clare Liguori): 'code review is the last manual review and approval a change receives before production' — after merge there are zero human gates. Stages: alpha/beta (functional+integration tests) → gamma (production-like, multi-region, same alarms + continuous canaries) → one-box (single VM/container/small % of Lambda invocations, ≤10% of regional traffic) → production in 5 waves (low-traffic regions first, AZ-by-AZ, then increasing parallelism across 24 regions/76 AZs). Mandatory bake time: ≥1h after each one-box, ≥12h after the first regional wave, 2-4h after later waves; global rollout ≈4-5 business days. Pipeline blockers: aggregate high-severity alarms halt promotion; time windows exclude nights/weekends/Fridays/holidays. Automatic rollback on one-box-scoped alarms, team-wide aggregate alarms (rolls back ALL of the team's in-flight regional deployments), and anomaly detection on request count/latency. Rolling deploys replace ≤33% of boxes keeping ≥66% capacity healthy. Ratchet origin story ('Going faster with continuous delivery'): commit-to-prod was 16 days with ~1.5h of real work; senior engineers catalogued historical release failures and converted them into best-practice checks embedded in Pipelines, rolled out warn-then-enforce; pilot achieved 90% cycle-time reduction; adoption by 'seduction' rather than mandate.

1ES (One Engineering System, est. 2014): a dedicated org standardizing the internal toolchain (Azure Boards, Azure Pipelines, 1ES Hosted Pools as the standard CI/CD substrate) — Microsoft dogfoods Azure DevOps/GitHub for ~all product engineering. SCM: rather than a bespoke server, Microsoft bent Git itself — VFS for Git virtualized the 300GB Windows monorepo, then was retired in favor of Scalar, whose features (partial clone, sparse-checkout, background maintenance, commit-graph) were progressively upstreamed into core Git (Scalar shipped in Git v2.38). Build: CloudBuild (ICSE 2016 paper) — distributed + caching build service: thousands of engineers, hundreds of codebases onboarded, content-based caching, 1.3x-10x build/test speedups, 99% availability, designed to tolerate non-deterministic build tools and under-declared dependencies; evolved into BuildXL (Build Accelerator) which verifies incrementality via observed runtime file accesses (sandboxed I/O observation) for the largest codebases (Windows, Office). Deployment: Azure Safe Deployment Practices (Russinovich): all code AND config changes flow through canary → pilot → progressively broader rings with centrally-defined mandatory health signals and mandatory bake times between stages; Gandalf (NSDI 2020) is an AIOps gate that statistically correlates fleet health anomalies with in-flight deployments and auto-stops/blocks them. Productivity: co-authored the SPACE framework (Forsgren, Storey, Zimmermann et al., ACM Queue 2021 — Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Communication/collaboration, Efficiency/flow), the canonical statement that no single metric measures developer productivity.

Far less public. Confirmed-but-undocumented internal systems: ODO (deployment orchestrator) and Shepherd (infrastructure/release management) — both leak into public view via oracle/terraform-provider-oci's ocibuild.conf ('publish_shepherd_providers', 'odo-artifacts-signed-generic-local' — note artifacts are signed). Public doctrine comes from Pradeep Vincent's 'First Principles' series: blast radius of server/rack/DC changes isolated to at most one fault domain at a time; electrical zones map 1:1 to customer-facing fault domains to prevent correlated failure; 'shrink-wrapped' region buildout automation let OCI stand up 28+ regions in under four years — region buildout itself is the pipeline product. Customer-facing OCI DevOps service (2021) reflects internal patterns: build pipelines keyed to commit IDs, artifact repositories, deployment pipelines with rolling/blue-green/canary strategies deployable across regions. Net: Oracle validates the same progressive-exposure + fault-domain-isolation doctrine but publishes no monorepo/CI internals; treat as confirmation of the deployment-safety convergence, not a source of build-fabric design.

convergent_patterns: Virtualized, lazily-materialized working copies for monorepo scale — all three monorepo operators independently built the same thing: Google CitC (FUSE overlay, <10 files per workspace), Meta EdenFS (checkout in seconds, fetch-on-access), Microsoft VFS for Git→Scalar/partial clone (upstreamed into Git). Full clones are abandoned as a concept at scale.

Two-tier verification with an explicit speed bias: a fast curated presubmit (Google ~11 min median, 95%+ predictive of full-suite pass; Meta diff-time Sandcastle; Microsoft gated CloudBuild builds) plus an exhaustive asynchronous postsubmit that batches changes, auto-bisects failing batches to find culprits, and auto-rolls-back (TAP) or files push-blocking tasks (Landcastle). Nobody runs all affected tests before merge; everybody accepts and engineers around post-merge breakage.

Dependency-graph-driven test selection as the core CI primitive: Google selects from a near-real-time global Blaze dependency graph; Meta layers ML on top (1/3 of affected tests, >99.9% regression catch); Microsoft CloudBuild/BuildXL skip via content caches. The build graph, not the CI config file, decides what runs.

Content-addressed caching + remote execution as the determinism substrate: Blaze/Forge, Buck2 RE (Bazel RE API compatible), CloudBuild/BuildXL content-based caching (1.3x-10x speedups), Brazil's reproduce-any-artifact-ever guarantee. Hermeticity/reproducibility is treated as a correctness property of the delivery fabric, not an optimization.

Code review is the LAST human gate; everything between merge and production is automated: Amazon states it verbatim (no human interaction post-merge, most deployments watched by no one); Meta Conveyor: 97% of container pipelines fully automated (55% deploy every change); Azure SDP: automated ring progression governed by central policy + Gandalf AIOps gate; Google TAP auto-rollback. Manual deploy approval is considered an availability risk, not a safety control.

Progressive exposure with mandatory bake time and health-gated automatic rollback, converged across 4+ companies: Amazon one-box→waves with ≥1h/≥12h/2-4h bakes and aggregate-alarm + time-window blockers; Azure canary→pilot→rings with mandatory health signals and bake times; Meta 2% canary→100% with push-blocking tasks; OCI one-fault-domain-at-a-time blast-radius doctrine; Google canarying (SRE Workbook). Bake time exists because slow-burn failures are a proven class.

Failures ratchet into platform-enforced checks (the ratchet doctrine): Amazon catalogued every historical release-failure cause and converted the list into best-practice checks embedded in Pipelines, rolled out warn-then-enforce; Azure encodes mandatory health signals/policies centrally; Meta converts failures into push-blocking tasks; Google converts breakage classes into presubmit analyzers (Tricorder) and auto-rollback. Incidents produce new automated gates, not new process documents.

The dev platform is a product owned by a dedicated org, adopted by being better, not by mandate: Google EngProd, Meta DevInfra, Microsoft 1ES (since 2014), Amazon Builder Tools ('seductive adoption'). One blessed pipeline/deploy tool replaces per-team scripts (Conveyor 'one-tool-fits-all', Apollo shared service, 1ES Hosted Pools).

Automated large-scale change tooling with ownership-sharded, pattern-auto-approved rollout: Google Rosie (shard by OWNERS, independent test-mail-submit per shard, global approvers auto-approve conforming shards); Meta codemod tooling + Butterflybot rules; Microsoft 1ES now applying agentic automation to fleet-wide compliance changes. Mass refactoring capability is the payoff that justifies the monorepo.

Productivity measured multidimensionally with surveys + behavioral logs, never one number: Google GSM/QUANTS, Microsoft/GitHub SPACE, Google DORA (lead time, deploy frequency, change-fail rate, MTTR), Meta's 7-year metrics study (FSE 2016) showing deploy frequency does not hurt productivity/quality.
divergences: Merge admission — optimistic vs pessimistic: Google admits after presubmit and relies on postsubmit batching + automated culprit-finding + auto-rollback (trunk is allowed to be transiently red, Build Cops + rollback-first culture absorb it); Meta's Landcastle is a pessimistic land queue that rebases and re-tests before landing, with push-blocking semantics keeping trunk shippable. Driven by scale: at >1 change/second Google cannot serialize; at lower rates queue-before-land buys an always-green trunk.

SCM substrate strategy: Google built a fully bespoke centralized service (Piper on Spanner) after concluding nothing commercial scaled; Meta forked/rewrote an existing DVCS (Mercurial→Sapling/Mononoke in Rust); Microsoft deliberately stayed on Git and upstreamed scale features (Scalar) to avoid a fork; Amazon rejected monorepo entirely (Brazil version sets over thousands of packages); Oracle appears to run conventional hosted SCM with bespoke deploy (ODO/Shepherd). There is no convergence on build-vs-bend-vs-buy for SCM — only on the virtual-checkout property.

Mono vs polyrepo: Amazon's version-set model achieves reproducibility and isolation without a monorepo, at the cost of expensive cross-cutting upgrades (shared-package rebuild storms) and no atomic LSCs; Google/Meta/Microsoft accept monorepo infrastructure cost to get atomic refactors and one source of truth.

Deployment cadence vs blast-radius posture: Meta deploys 55% of services on every change within minutes (consumer product, cell-light, fast rollback); Amazon/Azure deliberately stretch global rollout over ~a week of waves and bakes (infrastructure cloud where a bad change takes down customers' workloads); Oracle is the most conservative (one fault domain at a time). The product's blast radius, not engineering maturity, sets the cadence.

Test selection mechanism: Google trusts deterministic graph-based selection (requires near-perfect dependency declaration in Blaze); Meta uses probabilistic ML selection and accepts a statistical miss rate caught post-land. Meta's choice reflects a messier dependency graph and mobile build matrix; Google's reflects decades of enforced BUILD hygiene.

Build-system strictness: Bazel/Buck2 demand hermetic, fully-declared dependency graphs (greenfield rules languages); Microsoft CloudBuild/BuildXL was explicitly designed to tolerate non-deterministic legacy build tools and under-declared dependencies by observing file I/O at runtime (retrofit strategy for 30-year-old codebases). Choose strictness when you own the codebase from the start — Oyatie's situation.

What is public: Google/Meta/Microsoft publish papers and open-source the actual tools (Bazel, Buck2, Sapling, Scalar, BuildXL); Amazon publishes doctrine (Builders' Library) but keeps Brazil/Apollo/Pipelines closed; Oracle publishes almost nothing about the inner loop.
anti_patterns: Human approval gates in the deploy path post-code-review: Amazon explicitly removed all of them ('full CD' = no human interaction after merge); Azure SDP automates ring promotion; manual deployment approval is treated as theater that adds latency without safety.

Cherry-pick release branches: Meta retired branch+cherry-pick releases in 2017 for push-from-master with canary, at web scale; release branches survive only where regulatory/mobile-store constraints force them.

Running the full test suite presubmit: Google explicitly rejects it ('waiting a long time to run every test during code submission can be severely disruptive'); presubmit exhaustiveness is an anti-goal — fast+reliable subset only, with postsubmit + rollback covering the gap.

VFS for Git: built, operated, and retired by Microsoft — full filesystem virtualization of Git was abandoned in favor of Scalar/partial-clone/sparse-checkout upstreamed into stock Git. Lesson: prefer mechanisms that converge with upstream over permanent forks of the substrate.

Buck1 and Perforce: Meta threw away Buck1 and rewrote as Buck2 in Rust around a single incremental dependency graph; Google abandoned Perforce when it could not scale and CitC/Piper replaced it. Both retired systems that conflated too many concerns or hit architectural ceilings.

Noisy static analysis: Google removes any Tricorder analyzer whose 'not useful' click rate drifts above ~5-10%; compiler-error-level checks must be effectively zero-false-positive. Shipping a linter wall that developers ignore is an explicitly retired practice.

Per-team hand-rolled deployment scripts/pipelines: Apollo (2014) and Conveyor ('one-tool-fits-all', 30k pipelines) exist precisely to kill these; heterogeneous deploy tooling is treated as an incident-rate multiplier.
Single-number productivity metrics (LOC, commit counts, activity dashboards): rejected by Google's GSM/QUANTS and Microsoft's SPACE paper as measurement malpractice for knowledge work.

Under-declared dependencies silently tolerated: Brazil makes it structurally impossible (controlled link/classpaths); BuildXL detects via file-access observation; Bazel/Buck2 sandbox. Builds that 'work on my machine' are an enforced-away class.

Deploying during nights/weekends/Fridays without cause: Amazon's pipelines block these windows by default to protect on-call humans — 'deploy anytime' bravado is not the practice at the most automated shop in the industry.

Mandate-driven platform adoption: Amazon used warn-then-enforce and 'seductive adoption'; 1ES standardized by being better. Top-down forced migration without product quality is the documented failure mode.
oyatie_prescriptions: Make presubmit latency a published SLO of oya-ci: target ~10-15 min p50 (Google's measured 11-min average submit wait) with a curated, buck2-target-graph-selected fast suite; empirically tune so presubmit-pass predicts ≥95% full-suite pass. Everything slower runs postsubmit. Track 'selected tests per change' and bias the system to reward small changes, as TAP does.

Build the ADR-0513 Tide merge queue as a Landcastle-style pessimistic queue first (rebase + re-test against projected merge state before admission — Oyatie's commit rate makes always-green trunk affordable), but design the data model for TAP-style optimistic batching + speculation + automated bisection culprit-finding + auto-revert from day one, so the queue degrades gracefully into batching when admission latency rises. Auto-revert with high-confidence attribution is the non-negotiable piece — Google ships it, and it is what makes optimistic admission safe.

Treat the buck2 content-addressed delivery fabric (ADR-0516..0535) as the single source of CI truth: dependency-graph-based test selection (Google model) before any ML selection (Meta model — only worth it when graph selection saturates and test volume hurts). Instrument remote action-cache hit rate, queue wait, and selected-test counts as first-class fabric SLIs from the first service.

Adopt Amazon's pipeline doctrine verbatim as the deployment product: code review is the last human gate; after merge → integration env → production-like gamma with the same alarms/canaries as prod → one-box stage (map directly to ONE CELL per ADR-0341/0348 cell architecture) → waves across cells. Encode mandatory bake times (≥1h after one-cell, ≥12h after first wave, 2-4h per later wave for multi-tenant rollouts), aggregate-alarm blockers, time-window blockers, and automatic rollback on cell-scoped alarms + metric anomaly. Cells give Oyatie the wave/shard topology Amazon had to invent — use shuffle-shard placement as the blast-radius unit for deployment waves.

Institutionalize the ratchet doctrine in the governance pipeline: every incident/SEV review MUST emit at least one machine-enforced artifact — a new pipeline blocker, presubmit analyzer, postsubmit check, or deployment-gating alarm — registered as a governance artifact (fits the existing ADR/evidence-gate machinery in cloud-ci/gates). Roll out each new check warn-then-enforce with a dated enforcement deadline, exactly as Amazon did. Maintain a queryable ratchet inventory; a check with no incident lineage or no enforcement date is a smell.

Express deployment admission policy in Cedar (ADR-0243): bake-time satisfied, alarm state clear, time window open, wave ordering respected — all as Cedar policies evaluated by the deployment orchestrator. This dogfoods the policy engine on the highest-value internal surface and makes the ratchet inventory literally policy-as-code, something no hyperscaler has published (they use bespoke policy stores) — a defensible trailblazing claim.

Build ONE Conveyor-equivalent deployment orchestrator targeting k8s/Talos cells; ban per-service deploy scripts structurally (no prod credentials outside the orchestrator). Steering metric: percentage of pipelines fully automated with zero manual intervention — Meta's published bar is 97%; anything below ~90% means the pipeline product is failing its users.

For the Piper/CitC + Sapling SCM destination: the convergent, load-bearing property across Google/Meta/Microsoft is lazy materialization + a change journal, not the storage engine. Prioritize (a) virtual/sparse working copies with fetch-on-access, (b) a Watchman-style filesystem journal feeding buck2 (the proven Buck2-EdenFS integration), (c) stacked-diff review as the unit of change. Follow Microsoft's lesson: stay protocol-compatible with an upstream (Sapling's Git interop) rather than forking the universe before the scale forces it.

Tricorder-pattern static analysis: analyzers (clippy lints, Cedar policy lint, axum API-contract/backward-compat checks, SLO-config validation per ADR-0130) surface ONLY at review time as resolvable findings with a 'not useful' feedback button; enforce a <5-10% not-useful rate or the analyzer is auto-disabled. Reviewer evaluates the Amazon checklist on every change: test coverage, instrumentation, rollback safety, backward compatibility — because review is the last human gate.

Ship Rosie-class LSC tooling early (it is cheap at Oyatie's size and establishes the muscle): codemods sharded by ownership metadata, each shard through the normal Tide pipeline, with a 'global approver' role + pattern-based auto-approval for conforming shards. This is the mechanism that keeps a Rust monorepo's shared libs/ and Cedar schemas evolvable without coordination meetings.

Guarantee Brazil-grade reproducibility: every released artifact reconstructible from content-addressed inputs ('reproduce any artifact ever produced, produce any artifact with a known delta'), and sign artifacts in the fabric (OCI's ODO publishes signed artifacts). This is the technical precondition for safe single-tenant→multi-tenant migration: patching a tenant's pinned version with a known minimal delta.

Steer the platform by GSM/SPACE-style multidimensional metrics: behavioral (p50/p90 presubmit latency, time-to-land a diff, merge-queue wait, action-cache hit rate, deploy lead time, change-failure rate, rollback rate — DORA four keys fall out of this) plus a quarterly developer-experience survey. Use Google's GSM discipline: write the goal before choosing the metric, and refuse any single-number productivity score.

decision_matrix.decision: Build ONE Rust/axum IdP (oya/identity) split into a single-homed write control plane and a cell-replicated authn data plane: every credential is verifiable offline in the request hot path (short-lived signed JWT/JOSE validated against cell-local JWKS — never synchronous central introspection), with hard-partitioned 'domains' (Oracle identity-domains model) isolating a primordial operator domain from customer/tenant domains, each tenant a domain shuffle-sharded across cells per ADR-0341/0348. Passkeys/WebAuthn are v1 table stakes via the existing oya-shared-webauthn-server-kernel; revocation is event+policy-driven (CAEP channel ~15min SLO + Cedar issue-time cutoff condition), not blacklist.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: AWS IAM (global control plane + autonomous per-region data planes, offline SigV4 verify, irrevocable temp creds + policy-condition revocation), Microsoft Entra (single write primary per partition + geo-replicated read replicas + Backup Authentication System, CAE 15min revoke), Oracle OCI (converged identity-domains with Default operator-only domain), Google (offline ALTS/JWT verify, central session revocation), all five ship FIDO2 passkeys in product
decision_matrix.rationale: 5/5 converged: writes centralized + reads/validation local-and-offline; revocation as events/policy not per-request call-home (synchronous IdP dependency in every request path is a global SPOF). 5/5 ship passkeys; Google proved consumer scale (400M accounts, 1B+ sign-ins) and zero phishing across 85k employees. Offline verify + Cedar evaluate must be in-process per request to stay statically stable when the IdP control plane is down.

decision_matrix.decision: Embed the cedar-policy Rust crate as an IN-PROCESS PDP inside every axum service (no network hop in the decision path), unifying RBAC (principal-group claims resolved at token issuance) + ABAC (when/unless conditions) + ReBAC (entity parent hierarchy + per-resource policy templates) in Cedar per ADR-0243. A central control-plane policy-store service compiles/validates/versions/signs policy bundles and pushes them as content-addressed buck2 artifacts (ADR-0516..0535) to cells; tenant = Cedar namespace aligned to cells. Deny discipline: additive permits are routine, forbid reserved for the structural 'forbid unless resource.tenant == principal.tenant' cell-isolation invariant. Ship BatchIsAuthorized for list filtering; emit every allow AND deny as an audit event; gate every policy change on Cedar SMT/symbolic invariant analysis in oya-ci.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: AWS Cedar + Verified Permissions (OOPSLA'24: one language for RBAC+ABAC+ReBAC, 4-11us p99 embedded, 28-80x faster than OpenFGA/Rego; AWS documents both embedded-SDK and remote-PDP, recommends embedding when latency matters; Zelkova runs ~1B SMT queries/day), Google Zanzibar (local-replica checks, 99% never leave region, p95<10ms), Azure (deny-first, denies not user-authorable), OCI (allow-only, coarse analyzable language)
decision_matrix.rationale: 5/5 default-deny with order-independent set evaluation; 5/5 converged on roles-for-manageability + attributes-for-granularity + relationships-for-sharing; central policy distribution + distributed in-process evaluation is the converged topology (Cedar's own paper recommends embedding; remote PDP-as-product is orders of magnitude behind at ~200 TPS vs Zanzibar's 10M QPS). Policy-as-code with automated reasoning in CI is proven hyperscaler practice (Zelkova ~1B SMT/day), not research. ADR-0243 already ratifies Cedar.

decision_matrix.decision: Cell = one Talos-imaged k8s cluster + its own datastores/queues/observability, ZERO shared state with siblings (cluster-per-cell, the k8s control plane is itself a blast-radius boundary), with a published cap in three units (TPS, tenant count, storage GB) and a buck2 full-scale cell load test gating any limit change; never operate above ~70% of tested max. Cell router is the thinnest possible Rust/axum data-plane layer serving a content-addressed tenant->cell route table from last-known-good when the control plane is unreachable (NO per-request directory lookup). Bridge isolation: pooled cells with Cedar-enforced row-level tenancy for standard tiers, dedicated silo cells for premium/regulated/whale tenants; shuffle-shard tenants to k-of-n workers inside pooled cells. Tenant migration (clone->flip->redirect->forget) is a day-one state machine rehearsed weekly against synthetic tenants. Control plane is CP and allowed to fail; enforce a buck2 lint that data-plane targets may not link control-plane clients on the request path.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: AWS (cell-based whitepaper: capped self-contained cells, thinnest-possible router serving routes cached from S3, REL11-BP04 static stability, shuffle sharding ~730B shards, clone->flip->redirect->forget migration, Physalia cell-per-resource), Azure deployment stamps (>=2 stamps min, tenant-count capacity proxy, migration backplane warning), Google Borg cells + Spanner directory movement + quarterly Global Chubby planned outage, Meta Shard Manager solver-driven placement with graceful drain
decision_matrix.rationale: 5/5 converged on capped, fully self-contained, tested-max bulkheads (scale-out = add cells, never grow past tested limit); 3+ state CP/AP split with static stability almost verbatim; thin statically-stable global layer is universal (AWS reject smart-gateway-per-request shape that violates static stability). ADR-0341/0348 already anchor cells + autosharding; this operationalizes them.

decision_matrix.decision: Build exactly ONE platform-owned shell (oya/app-shell-frontend) owning ALL chrome (global nav, unified search, notifications, tenant/region/cell context, settings, theming, telemetry init, feature-flag bootstrap, and SOLE token brokerage). First-party modules use Google-style build-time composition from the buck2 monorepo (each module an independent buck2 target emitting a content-addressed bundle, composed via a versioned route-registration manifest) — NOT runtime iframes, NOT webpack module federation. The Oyatie design system is a first-class product with WCAG 2.1 AA / dark mode / RTL / i18n baked into components, enforced as a merge gate. Shell mints short-lived audience-scoped tokens per module request, audience bound to module identity in Cedar (modules structurally cannot call outside their declared audience). Ship AWS-style immutable multi-session (one tenant/role per tab) from the start. Reserve a sandboxed-iframe lane only for FUTURE third-party extensions.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: Google Cloud Console (retired iframe MFE, now complete build-time isolation, protobuf message contracts, no shared runtime deps), AWS (platform-owned Unified Navigation + Cloudscape design system as shell/module contract, manifest composition recommending web components not iframes, multi-session 5 identities), Azure Ibiza (shell-owned token brokerage: 3rd-party tokens encrypted so only ARM can use them; BladeFullReady<4s p80/<8s p95 admission gate), Meta Comet (tiered 50/150/300KB loading, per-product JS byte budgets enforced at merge)
decision_matrix.rationale: 5/5 put all cross-cutting chrome in one platform shell and forbid modules re-implementing it (strongest convergent signal); convergence AWAY from runtime iframes for first-party modules (Google retired, Azure escaping, AWS omits, Meta never used); 5/5 mandate one design system as the shell<->module contract; shell-owned token brokerage is universal. Build-time composition is the right fit for the buck2 monorepo (atomic commits make sharing the design system safe).

decision_matrix.domain: Control plane: uniform resource model + operation ledger + metering->billing
decision_matrix.decision: Ratify ONE uniform resource-provider contract NOW: a typed resource-schema registry in libs/ (built by buck2) where every single-concern microservice (ADR-0132) implements CRUDL handlers, enforced by a shared Rust contract-test crate gating cloud-ci (idempotent PUT, no duplicate create, read-after-write equality, stable pagination — extends cloud-control-plane-operation-contract.json). Build ONE Operations service ('operation ledger') with AIP-151 semantics (operations/{id}, three terminal states, structured errors, ~30-day retention, NO auto-rollback at this layer) sharded per cell. Mandate client-supplied UUID idempotency tokens (via existing oya-shared-idempotency-key-kernel). Hierarchy: tenancy -> nested compartments, exactly-one-parent, as the SINGLE attach point for Cedar policy + quota + cost. Two annotation systems: governed schema'd tags (policy/quota/cost-capable, inherited) vs free-form labels (reporting only). Admission-control gateway (oya/api-gateway, Google Service Control analog) does authn->Cedar authz->quota check->serve->emit one usage record, cell-local. Metering is a separate append-only exactly-once pipeline (usage->dedup->aggregate->rate-against-versioned-price-sheet->invoice) with explicit late-event window and native FOCUS 1.2 exports. Major-version-only API surfaces enforced by an api-linter + golden-schema-diff buck2 gate. Resource schemas codegen Terraform + KRM operator + Rust stubs + docs + contract tests.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: Google AIP corpus (AIP-122/151/155/128/180-185: uniform LROs, request_id idempotency, declarative-friendly resources, major-version-only) + Service Control admission+telemetry, Azure ARM Resource Provider Contract (mandatory uniform provider, provisioningState, idempotent PUT) + meter-id->rating->invoice pipeline, AWS Cloud Control API (JSON-schema handlers + contract-test suite, client-token idempotency, no auto-rollback) + 'APIs are forever' + FOCUS 1.0 exports, OCI work requests + declarative quota + cost-tracking tags, all four ship FOCUS
decision_matrix.rationale: Multiple 4-5/5 convergences: one machine-checked resource-provider contract every service implements; async-by-default mutations returning a first-class operation resource with uniform polling/terminal states; client UUID idempotency tokens; one hierarchical container that is the single attach point for identity/policy + quota + cost; governed tags split from labels; metering separated from rating separated from invoicing; FOCUS as universal billing interchange; no-breaking-changes major-version-only doctrine. Google/Azure prove enforcing from day one is far cheaper than AWS's 15-year Cloud Control retrofit.

decision_matrix.decision: Make the mandated OpenSLO files ({oya,cloud}/<service>/slos/*.openslo.yaml per ADR-0130) the SINGLE source from which alerting is codegenerated by a buck2 rule into the SRE-Workbook multiwindow multi-burn-rate set (page 14.4x/1h+5m, 6x/6h+30m; ticket 1x/3d+6h); cloud-ci rejects any hand-written static-threshold PAGING alert. Burn-rate alarms are the automatic-rollback trigger in the oya-ci/Tide promotion pipeline; deploy waves along cell topology with mandatory bake times; o11y and IdP/Cedar control planes ride the slowest wave. Standardize Rust/axum instrumentation on ONE structured wide event per unit of work (trace_id, cell_id, tenant_id, Cedar decision id, timers) and derive RED metrics from it after the fact. Two telemetry tiers: cell-local hot Prometheus-compatible TSDB (Gorilla compression, ~26h window, alert evaluation cell-LOCAL so partition can't blind paging) + columnar wide-event store (ClickHouse-class, 14-30d) for high-cardinality exploration. Cardinality is build-time enforced via the existing oya-check-metric-cardinality gate: tenant_id/user_id/request_id FORBIDDEN as metric labels; cell_id/region mandatory. OTLP/W3C is the ONLY external ingestion contract. Audit lane is a separate single-concern service (hash-chained signed digests to WORM, fixed >=365d, non-disableable) disjoint from ops logs. ORR is machine-readable in the governance pipeline; incidents feed it (COE/SEV closed loop).
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: Google (SRE Workbook multiwindow multi-burn-rate as terminal alerting doctrine, Monarch leaf-evaluated alerting survives partitions, Dapper; Cloud Monitoring IS Monarch — dogfood), AWS (alarm-triggered auto-rollback before human paged, one-structured-log-per-unit-of-work -> derived metrics, p99 not averages, ORR/COE closed loop, OTel primary, CloudTrail hash-chain integrity), Azure (Geneva two-tier hot/cold + hard cardinality caps with sentinel overflow, SDP rings+bake+Gandalf, Kusto dogfood), Meta (Gorilla 12x compression + Scuba for high-cardinality, Conveyor 97% automated HCS-gated), OCI (Audit fixed 365d, thousand-eyed canary)
decision_matrix.rationale: 5/5 metrics-gated progressive delivery with AUTOMATIC rollback; 5/5 wave/ring/cell blast-radius with mandatory bake; 5/5 two-tier hot-metrics-for-alerting + high-cardinality-event-store-for-exploration; 4+ hard cardinality enforcement (not advice); SRE burn-rate is the authored-and-productized paging doctrine; 4/5 OTel as external contract; 4+ separate immutable audit lane; 4+ closed-loop incident->readiness-checklist. The existing oya-check-metric-cardinality and oya-check-slo-coverage gates already encode this direction.

decision_matrix.decision: Two-tier verification on the buck2 fabric: presubmit latency a published oya-ci SLO (~10-15min p50, buck2-target-graph-selected fast suite tuned so presubmit-pass predicts >=95% full-suite pass) + exhaustive async postsubmit with automated bisection culprit-finding and auto-revert. Build ADR-0513 Tide as a Landcastle-style pessimistic merge queue first (rebase+re-test against projected merge state) but model TAP-style optimistic batching/speculation/auto-revert for graceful degradation. Adopt Amazon's pipeline doctrine verbatim: code review is the LAST human gate; after merge -> integration -> production-like gamma -> ONE-CELL one-box -> waves across cells with mandatory bake times (>=1h after one-cell, >=12h after first wave), aggregate-alarm + time-window blockers, automatic rollback. Express deployment ADMISSION policy in Cedar (bake-time satisfied, alarm clear, window open, wave order respected) — dogfooding the policy engine. Institutionalize the ratchet: every SEV review MUST emit a machine-enforced gate (new oya-check-* / blocker / alarm) registered in cloud-ci/gates, rolled out warn-then-enforce with a dated deadline; maintain a queryable ratchet inventory. ONE Conveyor-equivalent orchestrator for k8s/Talos cells; ban per-service deploy scripts (no prod creds outside it). Guarantee Brazil-grade reproducibility: every artifact reconstructible from content-addressed inputs + signed. Steer by GSM/SPACE multidimensional metrics + DORA four keys, never a single number.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: Google (TAP 50k changes/day 4B tests/day, ~11min presubmit predicting 95%+, postsubmit batching+auto-bisect+auto-rollback, Rosie LSCs, Tricorder <5% FP gate, GSM/QUANTS), Meta (Buck2 RE content-addressed, Predictive Test Selection 1/3 tests >99.9% catch, Landcastle land queue, Conveyor one-tool 97% automated, push-from-master), Amazon (review-is-last-human-gate, one-box->5 waves + bake times + aggregate-alarm/time-window blockers + auto-rollback, ratchet: failure-catalog->enforced-checks warn-then-enforce, Brazil reproduce-any-artifact), Microsoft (1ES single toolchain, SDP+Gandalf, SPACE), OCI (one-fault-domain-at-a-time, signed ODO artifacts)
decision_matrix.rationale: 5/5 two-tier verification with speed-biased presubmit + exhaustive async postsubmit (nobody runs all tests presubmit); 5/5 dependency-graph-driven test selection; 5/5 content-addressed caching + RE as determinism substrate; 4+ code-review-is-last-human-gate with everything post-merge automated; 4+ progressive exposure + bake + health-gated auto-rollback; the ratchet doctrine (incidents produce enforced gates not docs) is convergent across Amazon/Azure/Meta/Google. ADR-0513 Tide + ADR-0516..0535 buck2 fabric already anchor this; the rich existing libs/oya-check-* tree IS the ratchet inventory.

trailblazing_bets: Deployment admission policy expressed natively in Cedar (ADR-0243): bake-time-satisfied, alarm-state-clear, time-window-open, wave-ordering-respected are all Cedar policies evaluated by the deployment orchestrator. No hyperscaler has published policy-as-code for the deploy ratchet itself (they use bespoke policy stores) — this makes the entire ratchet inventory literally policy-as-code and dogfoods the PDP on the highest-value internal surface. Defensible trailblazing claim.

SCIM 2.0 as the NATIVE shape of the IdP user/group REST API (Oracle goes furthest among the five but still keeps a translation layer) — dogfooding SCIM as Oyatie's own API eliminates the provisioning translation layer entirely and is an audit-ready differentiator enterprises expect.

Sub-60s cross-cell revocation SLO with an explicit zookie-equivalent freshness-token contract from day one: every policy bundle and entity snapshot carries a monotonic version, PEPs report the version evaluated, decision caches key on (request-hash, policy-version) so policy pushes invalidate structurally not by TTL. p99 revocation enforcement <60s beats Azure CAE (~15min) and Google Cloud IAM (2-7min) — a trailblazing bar combining Zanzibar's causal-consistency token with AWS-style policy-condition revocation.

Agentic-primary delivery: the governance pipeline is built for AI agents as the primary author (isolated worktree -> protected PR -> Cedar/SLO-gated Tide admission -> reviewer-agent APPROVE), with ~24k/day automated-commit headroom (Google Piper ratio) designed in. Hyperscalers retrofitted automation onto human-primary pipelines; Oyatie's pipeline-as-product treats the agent as tenant zero of its own delivery fabric.

SLO files as the single codegen source for BOTH alerting (multiwindow burn-rate) AND deployment auto-rollback triggers AND the product's customer-facing SLO/error-budget primitives — one OpenSLO artifact drives internal ops, the CI gate, and the sold observability feature. The four clouds productized burn-rate alerting 2021-2026 but maintain it separately from their deploy gating; collapsing all three onto one artifact is beyond current practice.

Single resource schema codegenerating FIVE artifacts (Rust service stubs + Terraform provider + KRM/k8s operator + SDKs + docs + contract tests) from one source — Google/AWS codegen subsets, but a fully unified one-schema-five-artifacts pipeline on the buck2 fabric with the KRM operator as a first-class output (natural fit with the k8s+Talos substrate) exceeds any single hyperscaler's published toolchain.

Whole-substrate single-tenant 'realm' deployments (OCI realm model) made cheap via the content-addressed delivery fabric + Brazil-grade reproducibility: tenant data export/import is the migration clone step AND the data-residency/sovereign-enclave product tier, with per-tenant version pinning patched by known minimal delta. Owned-stack vendors can sell the whole substrate as a top tier; making it a routine reproducible artifact operation rather than a bespoke buildout is beyond current SaaS practice.
rejected_anti_patterns: Per-request online token introspection / synchronous central PDP on the hot path: a synchronous IdP or authz dependency in every request is a global SPOF. Evidence: Meta CATs designed specifically to avoid online auth dependencies in disasters; AWS irrevocable temp creds; Entra Backup Authentication System serving cached evaluations; Cedar embedded (4-11us) vs remote AVP (~200 TPS). Embed Cedar in-process; verify tokens offline against cell-local JWKS.

Long-lived static secrets for workloads (API keys, client secrets, stored root creds): AWS now programmatically deletes root credentials from member accounts; Azure managed identities + workload identity federation exist to eliminate secrets; OCI instance principals replace distributed keys. Workloads get platform-issued auto-rotated identity (cloud-secrets/cloud-kms); external systems enter via OIDC workload identity federation / RFC 8693.

Control plane on the request or recovery path: AWS REL11-BP04 forbids it; routers must serve last-known-good. Reject the Azure APIM-per-request-Cosmos-lookup smart-gateway shape — it violates static stability. The cell router serves a cached content-addressed route table and keeps routing through control-plane outage.

Runtime iframe micro-frontends + shared mutable deps for FIRST-PARTY console modules: Google built Cloud Console this way and RETIRED it ('not used anymore'); Azure's hidden-iframe Knockout remoting is acknowledged legacy. Use build-time composition from the buck2 monorepo; reserve sandboxed iframes only for future untrusted third-party extensions.

Unbounded metric cardinality: Azure/Geneva hard-cap series-per-metric with sentinel overflow rather than let the TSDB degrade; tenant_id/user_id/request_id as metric labels is the canonical failure. The existing oya-check-metric-cardinality gate enforces this at build time — high-cardinality questions go to the wide-event store, never metric labels.

Human approval gates in the deploy path after code review, and human-watched deployments: Amazon states code review is the last human gate (most deployments watched by nobody); Meta 97% of pipelines fully automated. Manual deploy approval is treated as an availability risk, not a safety control. Automatic alarm-triggered rollback replaces it.

Per-service non-uniform control planes and bespoke CRUD shapes: Azure retired classic ASM for ARM; AWS's heterogeneous APIs forced the expensive Cloud Control retrofit; Google wrote the AIPs to prevent recurrence. Ratify the uniform resource-provider contract before service #2 invents its own shape.

Synchronous long-running mutations blocking the request on provisioning: every provider moved to async-by-default with a first-class operation resource. ARM RPC and AIP-151 forbid blocking structurally.

Turing-complete / recursive policy languages and ordered first-match policy semantics on the hot path: Cedar deliberately omits recursion/loops for guaranteed termination + decidable SMT analysis (42-80x faster than Rego); all five use order-independent set evaluation with default-deny. No ad-hoc forbids for everyday revocation — revocation = remove the permit/group edge.

Static-threshold / average-based paging alerts: the SRE Workbook is structured as the progressive retirement of cause-based and static-target alerts in favor of multiwindow multi-burn-rate; Amazon alarms on p99/p99.9/p99.99 never averages. Cause-based alerts may exist but may not page.

Mixing audit and operational logging in one pipeline: every compliance-selling cloud keeps them separate services with independent immutability/retention (CloudTrail / Cloud Audit Logs always-on 400d / OCI Audit 365d). The audit lane is a separate single-concern service writing hash-chained signed digests to WORM; ops logs stay on cheap retention.

Per-team hand-rolled deploy scripts and one-tool-per-team: Meta Conveyor 'one-tool-fits-all' (30k pipelines) and Apollo exist to kill these; heterogeneous deploy tooling is an incident-rate multiplier. One orchestrator, no prod creds outside it.

Region/cell-pinned single-instance workforce SSO with no replica, and bolting IdP DR on later: AWS Identity Center's primary-region-only design and Cognito's June-2026 multi-region retrofit are cautionary tales. Do not region-pin the workforce SSO; design multi-cell survivability + backup-auth path from v1.

Big-bang enforcement of new policy/quota regimes: Meta runs Policy Zones in logging mode before enforcement; AWS rolls ratchet checks out warn-then-enforce. Every new policy class and CI gate ships in shadow/warn mode with a dated enforcement deadline.

Single-number productivity metrics (LOC, commit counts): rejected by Google GSM/QUANTS and Microsoft SPACE as measurement malpractice for knowledge work. Steer the delivery fabric by multidimensional behavioral metrics + DORA four keys + a periodic developer-experience signal.
prescription.dogfood_doctrine: "BOOTSTRAP ORDER breaks circular deps by applying the Delos rule: the store/service holding another service's config must NOT depend on the service it configures. Tier 0 (primordial, depends on nothing in the substrate): (a) a zero-dependency strongly-consistent control-plane state store per cell (Delos-class, small 5-9 node, the bootstrap root); (b) cloud-kms + an internal CA issuing short-lived workload x509 certs minted at pod start (Meta ICA / OCI instance-principal); (c) the IdP's primordial operator 'Default' domain authenticating ONLY operators via hardware-backed passkeys with >=2 sealed-offline FIDO2 break-glass credentials that bypass federation entirely. The IdP MUST NOT depend on any service that itself needs authn — it self-authenticates operators and verifies its own tokens offline; its config lives in the Tier-0 store, not in a service the IdP gates. Tier 1 (depends only on Tier 0): the Cedar policy-store control plane (authenticates operators via the IdP, but every PDP is EMBEDDED in-process so authorization never makes a network call to the policy store — policy bundles are content-addressed artifacts cached cell-locally, statically stable if the store is down); cloud-secrets (workloads get secrets via platform identity, never static keys). Tier 2: the uniform control plane / operation ledger + admission gateway (consumes IdP tokens + embedded Cedar + quota); the cell router (serves a content-addressed route table from last-known-good, depends on NOTHING live at request time). Tier 3: observability (tenant ZERO of the IdP, Cedar, quota, and billing — it authenticates via the IdP, authorizes via embedded Cedar, is metered/billed like a real tenant, and is meta-monitored from a DIFFERENT cell so it never observes only itself) and metering->billing (consumes the gateway's usage stream; billing availability is decoupled from serving — batch pipeline, not inline). Tier 4: every product module (oya/<vertical>) and the console shell, which consume IdP token brokerage, embedded Cedar, the resource contract + operation ledger, quota, observability instrumentation, and the billing meter. The delivery fabric (oya-ci/Tide on buck2) sits beside all tiers: it deploys every service, expresses its OWN admission policy in Cedar (dogfooding the PDP), gates on the SLO files (dogfooding observability), and is the first consumer of the content-addressed artifact substrate. Hard rule encoded as a buck2 dependency lint: no Tier-N service may link a live client of a Tier->=N service on its request/recovery path; the four primordial circular risks (IdP-needs-authz, policy-store-needs-authn, o11y-needs-everything, control-plane-needs-config-store) are each broken by an explicit ADR — embed-don't-call, self-authenticate, meta-monitor-from-elsewhere, Tier-0-zero-dependency-store."
open_questions: First vertical module: which product (oya/crm, oya/itsm, oya/hr, oya/healthcare-integration/emr, oya/financial-planning, etc.) is the v1 vertical that the unified shell + full cloud substrate is dogfooded against? This sets the first tenant archetype, the first real Cedar schema, and the first billing meters — a founder revenue/market call, not an architectural one.

Pessimistic-vs-optimistic merge-queue default: start Tide as a strictly-serial always-green Landcastle land queue (affordable at current commit rate) or invest up front in optimistic TAP-style batching+speculation+auto-revert (needed only past ~1 change/sec)? The choice trades engineering cost now against a re-architecture later; depends on the founder's projected agent/human commit volume in year one.

Cell boundary placement: cell-WITHIN-region (AWS, sells regional independence) vs region-IS-the-cell (Meta, one global product) vs whole-cloud realm (OCI, sells sovereignty). The research shows the driver is GTM posture, not engineering — which does Oyatie optimize for first: blast-radius isolation, global UX, or sovereign single-tenant enterprise sales?

Static shuffle-sharding vs continuous solver-based placement: AWS keeps assignment static/auditable; Meta/Google continuously re-solve for utilization/locality at the cost of an always-on powerful (and distrust-worthy) control plane. Start static (simpler, statically stable) and only adopt a solver when scale forces it — but the founder must confirm the utilization/cost trade-off is acceptable for the early cost structure.

Audit retention as platform duty vs customer responsibility: fixed-non-negotiable (OCI 365d, GCP 400d immutable) vs customer-configurable (AWS up to 10y). This is a compliance-positioning and cost decision tied to the target regulated verticals (healthcare/EMR in the tree implies HIPAA; financial implies SOX) — founder + compliance call.

Pricing/metering model for the first module: which dimensions are metered (seats, API calls, storage, compute-units, per-vertical events) and what is the price-sheet structure that the FOCUS-conformant invoice pipeline rates against? Founder business-model input the metering pipeline needs before it can rate anything.

SCM destination sequencing: the ratified anchors name Piper/CitC + Sapling as destinations with Microsoft Scalar as a transitional bridge — but the trigger condition and timeline for migrating OFF the current GitHub-substrate (per ADR-0363) to the bespoke virtual-checkout SCM is a scale/cost threshold the founder must set, since it is the single most expensive infrastructure bet.
